newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold bounced to end Friday above New York's overnight close on heavy overseas buying led by Japanese traders reacting to a falling dollar/yen and a sharp Tokyo stock market drop, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$358.70/359.20 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$357.80/358.20 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$42 higher at HK$3,314 a tael.
"There was buying from the Japanese on a softer dollar/yen and the falling stock market," said a trader at a local bullion firm.
European buying in afternoon trade boosted gold prices further and dealers said the market was looking to push past $360 per ounce.
Gold was seen trading in a range between $357.00 and $359.50 per ounce in the short-term.
Tael gold's U.S. dollar equivalent was at $359.30/80, with strong premiums remaining due to a persistent shortage of kilobars in Hong Kong and better demand.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to 0 from -4.00.
